about: The inventory of comic treatments for every current V1 role ability and shared game action: who sees each, what starts it, which approved view fields it reads, what it must never show, its art, its motion in five forms (normal, reduced, static, cancelled, and what it never replays) and its states. Delivered in focused slices; each entry says whether it is delivered or planned. Treatments draw from the approved crew cards, the full-body figures and the room scenes; mechanics and disclosure are the rules', never the art's.
sources: packages/contracts/src/lobby-identity.ts (public name and chosen character of a seat)
packages/contracts/src/staged-start.ts (the setup preview carries a role and no knowledge)
rules: A chosen character is a public appearance, independent of the role: any character may hold any role. No face, outfit, pose, color or public effect is tied to a role or a team.
A command receipt says registered, never a result: not damage, not healing, not delivery. A result is shown only when an authorized view or acknowledgment carries it.

Public motion uses confirmed public facts only (PHASE_CHANGED, PUBLIC_MOVE, PUBLIC_HEALTH_CHANGED and the public view). No public animation names a private target, an action type, a role, a weapon or an action's source.

Private art is drawn only inside the seat's own open private sheet or its own action strip, never on the shared display, a host view or another phone. Every player phone loads all private art in one stylesheet, whatever its role, so loading says nothing.

Unordered sets stay unordered: the Insider's three candidates, the Code's four players and a Code submission are shown in seat order, a public order, never in an order the view or the engine might carry.

Every effect has a normal form, a reduced-motion form, a static fallback and a cancelled state. Motion never delays a control, pauses a timer or decides game state. Changing the reduced-motion setting cancels movement at once and leaves the latest authoritative pose, health and location.
A duplicate event, a receipt recovery or a reconnection never replays an effect as a new action.
No secret-specific sound or haptics. No historical optional power and no new ability.

treatments.title: Insider: the investigation board
treatments.trigger: The player opens their card during gameplay. The view carries the three candidates from the first gameplay view; the setup reading stage's preview carries none, so nothing is shown before gameplay.
disclosure: The three portraits in seat order (a public order), whatever order the view lists them in.
The three role names as one set in one envelope, in a fixed order that never changes with the candidates, below all three portraits and beside none of them, in every layout (large text included).

Nothing ties a role name to a portrait: the same frame, pin, query tag, seat sticker and tilt-by-position for every portrait; one string around the whole set; no per-portrait color, line, animation order, accessible name or asset.
Inspecting a portrait lifts it and says that player's public facts (room, health, Captain, Jail), which every screen shows; it never adds evidence.
No sound and no vibration.
Never on the board, the shared display or a host view; not during setup.
treatments.concept: A cork board in the private sheet: three snapshots of the players' own crew cards pinned on a string in seat order, each with the same seat sticker in the portrait's corner, the name on the frame's margin and the same paper query tag; below, an open envelope holding a slip with three label tapes, Undercover, Alien and Cracker, stamped ONE EACH; one string pinned round the four corners of the whole set; a CLASSIFIED stamp on the file's tab; under it all, Who is which: unknown. People are written by hand on paper; roles are label tapes: two visual languages that never pair up.

motion.normal: The first open in a page assembles the file in 1020 ms: the board rises (180), the snapshots drop and are pinned in seat order (from 120, 70 apart, 260 each), the envelope rises (300) and its slip slides up with the three names together (520), the query tags swing on together (540), the corner pins pop and the string draws round the whole set (640, 380), the stamps land (CLASSIFIED 220, ONE EACH 860). Later opens show it at rest. Inspecting lifts the snapshot from its pin toward the middle (200 ms) while the rest dims; the inspect card lies over the dimmed envelope; Back or Escape returns it.
motion.reduced: The file appears at rest with an 80 ms fade. Inspecting rings the snapshot instead of lifting it.
motion.static: Without the ability art: the same file in paper and ink, words on plain paper, a plain envelope. Without the crew cards: the seat number large in each window (the corner sticker waits for the portraits).
motion.cancel: Closing the card, the page going to the background, the view going out of date or reduced motion being switched on finishes every animation at once and leaves the file at rest; nothing is replayed.
motion.replay: The assembly is a reveal the player asked for, not a game event: it plays once per page, on the first deliberate open, and never on an update, a recovery or a reconnect.

states: closed (no private word in the page)
inspecting one portrait (Show on board, Back)
show on board (the card closes; a ring on the own board for 1.6 s)
twelve-character names (a small snapshot ends a long name in an ellipsis; the button and the inspect card say it whole)
large text (one column: each snapshot with its number and whole name beside it, the envelope below the three; the card scrolls)
reduced motion (a fade; inspecting rings the snapshot)

accessible: <names> hold the roles Undercover, Alien and Cracker, one each. You are not told which of them holds which. (the release's sentence)
Their roles, one each: Undercover, Alien and Cracker. Which of them holds which is not known.

dependencies: The view's insiderCandidates is sorted by seat ID today (packages/engine/src/full-game/roster.ts); DSN-REQ-14 asks the contract to state that order, so no consumer can ever leak a role order through it.

treatments.title: Any role: the hidden card
treatments.trigger: The player presses Card while the card cannot be shown: the view is out of date or the turn's time is up. (Going to the background or out of date closes an open card at once, the reviewed conceal rule, and coming back shows the board; a page that opens in the background with its card open shows the folder.)
disclosure: One closed folder and the same words for every role and seat: nothing names or colors a role. Nothing private is in the page until the player opens the card again.
treatments.concept: A closed manila folder with a blank label and a clasp, where the card was.

motion.normal: None: the private content is removed at once.
motion.static: A plain paper rectangle with the words.
motion.replay: Opening the card again never replays a private cue.

states: pressed while out of date or time is up: the closed folder, no control
a page opened in the background: the closed folder with Show my card
back from the background: the board, the card closed; pressing Card opens the file again at rest, not assembled again

visible: Your card stays hidden until your view is up to date.

treatments.title: Hacker: the known Undercover
treatments.trigger: The player opens their card during gameplay. The view carries the known Undercover from the first gameplay view; the setup reading stage carries none.
disclosure: One snapshot, the known Undercover, from the view's knowledge.undercoverSeatId.

Of the Code, only what the rule itself gives the Hacker from the start: “Knows only who Undercover is and therefore knows that player's number is excluded from Code” (v2.1 roles.Hacker.starting_knowledge; Code.undercover_number_always_excluded). Nothing else is worked out.
treatments.concept: The same file kit: one snapshot of the known Undercover pinned on a string, the label tape UNDERCOVER on its frame (here the pairing is the Hacker's own knowledge), and beside it the Code's mark struck out: not in the Code. Under it, the Scans: one torn printout each, in the view's order.

motion.normal: The first open in a page assembles the file in about 1.1 s: the board rises, the snapshot drops and is pinned (120 to 380), the label tape slaps on (380, 180), the struck Code mark lands (520), the printouts feed in in the view's order (from 600, 90 apart, 240 each), the string draws (640, 380), CLASSIFIED lands (220). Later opens show it at rest; a Scan result that arrived since is printed once (420) with its stamp (140).
motion.reduced: At rest with an 80 ms fade; a new result fades in once; inspecting rings the snapshot.
motion.static: Without the ability art: paper and ink, plain printouts, a ruled Code mark. Without the crew cards: the seat number in the window and in each chip.
motion.cancel: As the Insider's file: closing, the background, an out-of-date view or reduced motion finishes everything at rest.
motion.replay: Once per page on a deliberate open; a result is printed once, the first time it is seen, never again on an update, a recovery or a reconnect.

states: large text (one column, the label as words)

visible: Not in the Code (proposed: the release's sentence names only the Undercover)

treatments.title: Hacker: Scan
treatments.trigger: The Hacker opens Scan from the Actions tray, picks a character on the board (themself included) and a faction guess, and confirms.
fields: knowledge.scanResults[]: round, targetSeatId, guess, matched, inCode
disclosure: The result is the view's knowledge.scanResults entry, never inferred from the receipt.
A wrong guess shows no Code information.
A right guess shows membership only, never a position.
The scan cue plays on the Hacker's own board only.
treatments.concept: In the Hacker's strip: the picked player's portrait chip beside the question, the three faction answers inline; while the Scan is on its way a scanner line sweeps the chip; registered is the same neutral stamp as every action. The result arrives in the Hacker's file as a printout: WRONG (nothing of the Code) or RIGHT with the Code's mark, plain for in the Code, struck for not in the Code.

motion.normal: The sweep runs (900 ms, back and forth) only while the Scan is on its way; the result is printed in the file once (420 ms) with its stamp (140 ms).
motion.reduced: No sweep: the target chip is ringed while sending; the result fades in once.
motion.static: The chip, the words and the stamp.
motion.cancel: A newer view, the strip closing, the background or reduced motion ends the sweep at once.
motion.replay: A result already shown is never printed again after an update, a recovery or a reconnect.

states: result: right, not in the Code

treatments.title: Hacker: Code submission
treatments.trigger: Round 5: the Hacker opens Code, picks four characters on the board and confirms.
disclosure: The four picks are an unordered set: shown in seat order, never as positions 1 to 4.
Registration is not a result: Code victory is checked with the other victories after normal Round 5 effects (V1-08).
treatments.concept: In the Hacker's strip: a punch card with four round windows. Each pick clips its portrait chip into a window, the windows filled in seat order whatever the picking order; on the board every pick wears the same check, never a number; the strip names the picks in seat order. Registered punches the card once; it is not a result.

motion.normal: The new pick's chip clips in (160 ms), the others stay put; registration punches the card (220 ms).
motion.reduced: No clip or punch: the chips appear; the neutral stamp says registered. Switching to reduced finishes a clip or punch at once.
motion.static: The card with its chips, or the words in seat order.
motion.replay: Never: not on a duplicate snapshot, a public fact about someone else, a recovery or a reconnect. Only a new pick clips, only the receipt punches.

states: picking 0 to 4 (the card filling in seat order)
a short phone (the card small at the start of the detail line)
dependencies: DSN-REQ-14: knowledge.code in seat order, stated in the contract (the submission's own order carries no meaning: SUBMIT_CODE.seatIds is a set).

treatments.title: Alien: the Code from the start
treatments.trigger: The player opens their card during gameplay.
fields: knowledge.code (four seats, the Alien among them)
disclosure: Four snapshots as one unordered group in seat order; no positions, no numbering beyond seat numbers.
treatments.concept: The same file kit: the four snapshots two by two, in seat order, one string round the four and the Code's tag (a punch card with four holes in a square) hanging from it; the Alien's own snapshot marked YOU; under it, Four players, in no order.

motion.normal: The first open in a page assembles the file in about 1.1 s: the board rises, the four drop in seat order and are pinned, the string draws round the four (520, 380), the Code's tag swings on (820, 260), CLASSIFIED lands (220).
motion.reduced: At rest with an 80 ms fade; inspecting rings the snapshot.
motion.static: Paper and ink; the seat numbers in the windows without the crew cards.

accessible: The Code is these four players: <names>. (the release's sentence, in seat order, the own marked (you))

dependencies: DSN-REQ-14: knowledge.code in seat order, stated in the contract.

treatments.title: Cracker: Rescue
treatments.trigger: The Cracker opens Rescue, picks a character (an Injured one in the Hospital from Room A or B, or themself while Injured, V1-05) and confirms; at the end of the round the public view may show the target Healthy.
fields: PUBLIC_HEALTH_CHANGED (Healthy) and PUBLIC_MOVE out of the Hospital
disclosure: Registering is not a recovery: the receipt is the neutral Registered stamp and the release's words; nothing in the strip or the card says the target is, or will be, healed.

The vials are the view's count of the two Rescues a match gives; one is drawn empty when the count falls (the use is reserved at acceptance and kept whatever the round brings, V1-15), never ahead of it.
A recovery is the public health change at the end of the round, drawn by the same status cue on every screen, naming no rescuer and no Rescue.
treatments.concept: In the Cracker's strip: the picked player's chip in a medical cross ring beside the question, and two vials at the start of the detail line, as many full as the view's count. On the receipt the vial that the count gave up drains once. In the card, while one is left, a slip with the vials and the release's sentence, Rescues you have left: N. Nothing on the board but the neutral targeting every action has.

motion.normal: When the view's count falls while the receipt shows, the emptied vial drains (240 ms). Nothing else moves.
motion.reduced: No drain: the vial is simply empty.
motion.static: The ring, the vials and the words.
motion.cancel: As every strip; reduced motion finishes a drain at once.
motion.replay: Never: the drain plays for the fall of the count, once; a duplicate snapshot, a recovery or a reconnect draws the vials at rest.

states: none left (no Rescue offered; the card says nothing, as the release)
choosing (a player in the Hospital from Room A or B, or yourself while Injured)
registered (one vial empty; not a recovery)
recovered later (public: a health change on every screen)

treatments.title: Blue Disabler and Red Disabler: Disable
treatments.trigger: The Disabler opens Disable, picks a character in the same location and confirms; one use per match.
fields: legalTargets.DISABLE (offered only while the one use is unspent)
disclosure: The Blue and the Red Disabler see the same strip, part for part: no color, class, asset or word differs. Each one's identity stays in its own role card (the approved device), so a glance at a phone mid-Disable tells nobody which.
The receipt spends the one charge (reserved at acceptance, V1-15) and is not a result: the target's chip is ringed by sparks at its corners, never struck.
The effect is public only as a health change at the end of the round, the same as any damage, from no direction.
treatments.concept: In the strip: the picked player's chip in a charged reticle (a dashed ring with four sparks at its corners) beside the question, and one charge cell at the start of the detail line, full while the server offers the Disable and spent on its receipt. The card draws no lasting spent cell: the view does not carry one (DSN-REQ-15).

motion.normal: On the receipt the cell discharges (200 ms).
motion.reduced: No discharge: the cell is simply spent.
motion.static: The reticle, the cell and the words.
motion.cancel: As every strip; reduced motion finishes a discharge at once.
motion.replay: Never: the discharge plays for the receipt, once.

states: registered (the charge spent; not a result)
spent later (not offered; no lasting mark until the view carries one, DSN-REQ-15)
dependencies: DSN-REQ-15: a lasting own field for the spent Disable (disablerAvailable means a legal target now).

treatments.title: Supplier: Supply
treatments.trigger: Round 3: the Supplier opens Supply, picks two different characters in the same location (themself allowed) and confirms; the delivery is acknowledged after the round's distribution.
disclosure: The two picks are a set: drawn and named in seat order, never first and second.
Registration is not delivery: the receipt ties the two tags and stamps Registered; nothing says a weapon arrived.

A delivery is shown only from an own acknowledgment (V1-16): the Supplier's slip names the players who received a weapon, in the release's sentence; a recipient's slip says one ordinary weapon arrived and names no Supplier. No public weapon marker.
treatments.concept: In the strip: two shipping tags at the start of the detail line, each pick's chip in a tag, in seat order; the receipt ties them together with a string. In the card, after Round 3: Supply results (the release's heading) with a slip per acknowledgment, its words the release's, a tag per player it names, and the stamp DELIVERED when a weapon arrived. A slip drops in once, the first time the card shows it.

motion.normal: A pick clips into its tag (160 ms); the receipt ties the tags (200 ms); a slip shown for the first time drops in (260 ms).
motion.reduced: No clip, tie or drop: the tags and slips appear at rest.
motion.static: The tags, the slips and the words.
motion.cancel: As every strip; reduced motion finishes a beat at once.
motion.replay: Never: a slip already shown in this page is drawn at rest; a duplicate snapshot, a recovery or a reconnect plays nothing.

states: second pick (the tags in seat order)

visible: Two players get a weapon each. Choose the first.
Supply for Player 1 and Player 8 registered.
Your Round 3 Supply granted one weapon each to Player 1 and Player 8.
You received one ordinary weapon from Supply in Round 3.

dependencies: DSN-REQ-14: successfulRecipientSeatIds in seat order, stated in the contract (the engine sorts them).

treatments.title: Undercover: Protection
treatments.trigger: The Undercover opens Protection, picks a Healthy or Injured character (themself included) and confirms.
disclosure: Grant, activation and consumption are drawn only for the Undercover (V1-17). The recipient never sees a shield; nothing public changes.
treatments.concept: The dome emitter device: a dome sketched over the picked portrait in the Undercover's file; queued (dashed dome, Active from round N), active (solid dome), consumed (dome cracked, Used).

motion.normal: Dome draw 300 ms on registration; crack 240 ms when the view says consumed.
motion.replay: A consumed dome never cracks again after recovery.

treatments.title: Ordinary shot (every eligible role)
roles: any holder of a supplied weapon, the Alien included
treatments.trigger: A seat whose view offers REGISTER_SHOT picks a character in the same location and confirms. Direct targeting only: no third player.
disclosure: Registration is not damage.
The public hit (cue-public-hit, a proposal) is the same for every cause and from no direction.
treatments.concept: A shared shot strip: a crosshair over the picked character on the own board, the weapon pip spent on registration. The same component for every role; the Officer's card and the supplied weapon differ only in their own private art.

motion.normal: Crosshair lock 180 ms; pip spends 160 ms on the receipt.

treatments.title: Officer: the one shot
treatments.trigger: Nine-player mode only. From Round 1, during the Officer's own ordinary turn; one ordinary shot in the match, never a second from a supplied weapon.
disclosure: The same shared shot strip; the sidearm device with one cell, empty once spent.
treatments.concept: The sidearm device's single cell in the strip; spent: the cell dark and a SPENT tag on the card.

motion.normal: As the ordinary shot.

treatments.title: Alien: shared actions and a supplied weapon
treatments.trigger: The Alien's view offers the shared actions; a weapon arrives only through a Supplier grant, and is used in Rounds 4 and 5 like any ordinary weapon.
disclosure: The supplied weapon slip in the Alien's file only; no public weapon marker.
treatments.concept: The ordinary shot strip; the weapon slip in the file.

motion.normal: As the ordinary shot.

treatments.title: Character selection
treatments.trigger: Setup: 30 seconds to choose; an unconfirmed choice is assigned automatically.
disclosure: A clean nine-character matrix; a taken character says who took it; nothing about roles exists yet.
treatments.concept: The nine crew cards in a 3 x 3 matrix on paper; a taken card gets the taker's seat stamp; the own pick pops and is ringed.

motion.normal: Pick pop 220 ms; taken stamp 120 ms.
motion.cancel: The timer closing settles every card.

visible: the release's words (compact-phone decision of 8 October 2026)

treatments.title: Private role-card reveal
treatments.trigger: Setup: the role card is turned by the player; at least 30 seconds of reading, then every player Ready.
disclosure: The card centers on the role; the device is added to the player's own character. No starting knowledge in this stage.
treatments.concept: The approved card turn (cue-role-card-turn) with the role device sliding into the character's hand.

motion.normal: The reviewed turn (220 ms) plus the device slide (180 ms).

treatments.title: Movement and room arrival
treatments.trigger: Tapping an eligible room's name tag (never an action-menu choice); the public move cue on PUBLIC_MOVE.
disclosure: The same walk for every move, transfer and release.
treatments.concept: The board-motion move (get up, walk, settle) and the room tags; arrival dust.

motion.normal: cue-public-move (900 ms).
motion.reduced: 80 ms fade at the new place.
motion.cancel: A newer move or a reconnect.

treatments.title: Action selection, targeting and confirmation
treatments.trigger: Actions tray, then the characters on the board, then the strip's confirmation.
disclosure: What can be chosen is only what the view offers; registered is not a result.
treatments.concept: The board-motion tray and strip, with each action's icon and device art added (slices 2 to 4).

motion.normal: The board-motion cues (tray, strip, eligible, picked, sending).

treatments.title: Standard Hack request and conversation
treatments.audience: request private; phase public; partner private to the two
treatments.trigger: A Hack is requested within the ordinary minute; its own 60-second conversation follows.
disclosure: The public sees a Hack phase; who with is known to the two only.
treatments.concept: A comms-line cable between the two portraits in each partner's own file; a public HACK banner over the board.

motion.normal: Cable draws 300 ms; banner 220 ms.

treatments.title: Pass turn
treatments.trigger: The central Pass button during the player's own ordinary turn (PASS-01).
disclosure: Role-neutral: the same for every seat.
treatments.concept: The center dock button: a stamped PASSED tab, then the turn accent moves on.

motion.normal: Stamp 120 ms.

treatments.title: Captain election, Jail vote, release choice and release vote
treatments.audience: own ballot private until the tally; tally public
treatments.trigger: The 60-second vote windows (V1-09, V1-10, V1-11).
disclosure: Ballots stay private until the published tally.
treatments.concept: Ballot slips dropped into a box over the board; the tally as chalk marks under each candidate's portrait.

motion.normal: Slip drop 260 ms; tally chalk 40 ms a mark.
motion.replay: A tally shown once is not re-chalked after recovery.

treatments.title: Injury, elimination and recovery; Hospital, Jail and Command transitions
treatments.trigger: PUBLIC_HEALTH_CHANGED and PUBLIC_MOVE; faction reveal at elimination.
disclosure: One hit for every cause and from no direction (cue-public-hit, a proposal, DSN-D35). Recovery names no rescuer.
treatments.concept: The board-motion hit and falls; a bandage coming off on recovery; the Jail door slam and the Command Room hatch as transition cues.

motion.normal: cue-public-hit, cue-public-move, cue-status-change.

treatments.title: Final Showdown
treatments.trigger: No winner after Round 5: everyone left moves to the Final Zone and registers one special shot.
disclosure: Targets are secret until resolution; shots resolve in Round 5 order.
treatments.concept: A two-row standoff in the Final Zone; each player's own crosshair; the public resolution one hit at a time.

motion.normal: The public hits in order.

treatments.title: End of game: roles, the Code and the outcome
treatments.trigger: phase.kind FINISHED with result and endReveal; ABORTED shows no winner and no reveal.
disclosure: Exact roles and the Code only through the finished-game reveal; an abort fabricates no winner and reveals no secret.
treatments.concept: Every character's card flips to show its device; the Code's four snapshots pinned in seat order; the winning team's banner.

motion.normal: Cards flip in seat order 120 ms apart.

treatments.title: Unavailable actions, rejection, missing assets and reconnecting
treatments.trigger: An action the view does not offer; a rejected receipt; a bundle that did not load; a reconnect.
disclosure: Reasons are the receipt's codes only; nothing is guessed.
treatments.concept: A NOT ACCEPTED stamp, an out-of-date banner, a closed folder for private content, paper-and-ink fallbacks.

motion.normal: Stamp 120 ms.
